rationale: Read complete driver and production entry. Actual transformed message handler, queue lanes and pending/controller/cancelled registries execute in separate VM contexts; imported collaborators are stubbed for firstPrompt only. In-memory before removes one uniquely required pending guard. Current Linux run passes both 1,000-request phases and independent final counts; this proves numeric cancellation-entry lifetime, not retained bytes or full worker transport behavior.

cases.title: baseline transform requires exactly one pending-membership guard
cases.reason: Rejects changed guard multiplicity and residual transformed imports before execution; source hashes record both actual in-memory variants.

cases.title: before: 1,000 completed requests followed by matching late cancellations
cases.reason: Actual request handler settles each synthetic firstPrompt before matching cancel arrives. Independently require 1,000 result messages, no pending/controllers and exactly 1,000 retained cancelled IDs; removes all process listeners in finally.

cases.title: after: 1,000 completed requests followed by matching late cancellations
cases.reason: Same exact production entry and stubbed import ports retain zero cancelled IDs with all result/pending/controller counts independently checked. Failure, running/queued cancellation and shutdown paths are outside this proof.
